title: Irrational Numbers and Recurring Decimals
seo_title: Year 8 Irrational Numbers Worksheets: Terminating and Recurring Decimals, Rational and Irrational Numbers (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: recognise irrational numbers in applied contexts, including square roots and π
meta_desc: Free Year 8 maths worksheets on rational and irrational numbers for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M8N01, AC9M8N03): terminating and recurring decimals, recurring decimals as fractions, square roots and π. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Rational numbers terminate or recur. Irrational numbers never end and never repeat.
key_sub: π and √ of a non-square whole number are irrational. A fraction terminates only if its denominator has just 2s and 5s.
body_html:
How it works

A rational number can be written as a fraction of two integers. Its decimal either terminates (0.375) or recurs (0.3 = 0.333…). A bar shows the repeating block: 0.27 = 0.272727…

A fraction in simplest form terminates only when its denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5.

An irrational number has a decimal that never ends and never repeats, so it cannot be written as a fraction. Examples are π and the square root of any whole number that is not a perfect square, such as √2. 3.14 and 227 are only approximations of π.

Example

Write 56 as a decimal.

5 ÷ 6 = 0.8333…

Answer: 0.83

Example

Write 0.45 as a fraction.

Let x = 0.4545… so 100x = 45.4545…

99x = 45, so x = 45/99.

Answer: 511

Example

Is √36 rational?

√36 = 6.

Answer: Yes

Common mistakes

  • Thinking every square root is irrational: √49 = 7 is rational.
  • Thinking a long decimal on a calculator must be irrational. 2 ÷ 3 = 0.6 is rational.
  • Writing 13 as 0.3. It is 0.3.
  • Using 3.14 or 227 as the exact value of π.

faq.a: A number that cannot be written as a fraction of two integers. Its decimal never ends and never repeats, like π or √2.
Yes. Every recurring decimal can be written as a fraction, for example 0.333… = 1/3.

faq.q: How can I tell if a fraction gives a terminating decimal?
faq.a: Simplify it. If the denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5, the decimal terminates; otherwise it recurs.
No. 22/7 and 3.14 are close approximations, but π is irrational, so no fraction is exactly equal to it.

sets.title: Square roots and π in context

items.q: A square has an area of 2 m². How long is each side?
items.e: Side × side = 2, so the side is √2 m ≈ 1.41 m, an irrational number.

items.q: A square has sides of 1 m. How long is its diagonal?
items.e: By Pythagoras, 1² + 1² = 2, so the diagonal is √2 m.

items.q: Between which two whole numbers does √50 lie?
items.e: 7² = 49 and 8² = 64, so √50 is between 7 and 8.

items.q: Between which two whole numbers does √20 lie?
items.e: 4² = 16 and 5² = 25, so √20 is between 4 and 5.

items.q: Which is the best estimate of √30?
items.e: 5² = 25 and 6² = 36; 30 is about halfway, so √30 ≈ 5.5 (it is 5.477…).

items.q: Which of these is exactly equal to π?
items.e: π is irrational, so no fraction or terminating decimal is exactly π.

items.q: A circular garden has a diameter of 10 m. Which is the exact circumference?
items.e: C = πd = 10π m. 31.4 m is only an approximation.

items.q: Which list contains only rational numbers?
items.e: Each of 0.5, −3, 27 and 0.3 can be written as a fraction: all rational.

items.q: Mia says 3.14159265 is irrational because it has many decimal places. Is she right?
c: No, it terminates, so it is rational
items.e: It stops after 8 decimal places, so it equals 314159265/100000000: rational.

items.q: Which fraction gives a recurring decimal?
items.e: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3 has a factor of 3, so 512 = 0.416 recurs.

items.q: Which fraction gives a terminating decimal?
items.e: 40 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5, so 740 = 0.175 terminates.

items.q: What is 17 as a decimal?
items.e: 1 ÷ 7 = 0.142857142857…, so the block 142857 repeats: 0.142857.

items.q: How many digits are in the repeating block of 17?
items.e: 17 = 0.142857: 6 digits repeat.

items.q: A calculator shows 0.6666666667 for 2 ÷ 3. Why does the last digit show 7?
c: The calculator made a mistake in the 6s
items.e: 23 = 0.6 forever; the screen has to round the last digit.

items.q: Which number lies between 3 and 4?
items.e: 3² = 9 and 4² = 16, so √10 is between 3 and 4: √10.

items.q: Order from smallest to largest: π, √10, 3.1
Is 0.9 equal to 1?
c: No, it is a bit less than 1

items.q: A cube has a volume of 20 cm³. Its edge length is ∛20 cm. Which is the best estimate?
items.e: 2³ = 8 and 3³ = 27, and 20 is close to 27, so ∛20 ≈ 2.7 cm (2.714…).

items.q: Which is irrational?
items.e: √16 = 4, √0.25 = 0.5 and √(9/4) = 1.5 are rational. √12 is not a perfect square, so it is irrational.

items.q: A running track has a circular end of radius 36.5 m. Why is the length of its curve not a whole number of metres?
c: It involves π, which is irrational
items.e: Length = π × 36.5, and multiplying by π gives an irrational number: it involves π.
